findings.title: HTTP error logging exposes proxy credentials
findings.problem: A supported URL such as https://proxy.example/arr?token=proxy-secret passes InstanceConfig validation and reaches validate_connection through startup.py:154–160. On a 502 response, the newly logged HTTPStatusError includes the request URL and proxy-secret (verified with installed HTTPX). collect_secrets only collects API keys and auth secrets, so neither logging sink redacts this URL token. Previously this branch logged only the status code; now the credential reaches stderr and the web log buffer.
findings.why_it_matters: A supported URL such as https://proxy.example/arr?token=proxy-secret passes InstanceConfig validation and reaches validate_connection through startup.py:154–160. On a 502 response, the newly logged HTTPStatusError includes the request URL and proxy-secret. collect_secrets only collects API keys and auth secrets, so neither logging sink redacts this URL token.
findings.fix_hint: Keep logging the status code instead of the raw exception, or explicitly strip credentials and query values before logging. Add a regression test using a configured URL token and a 502 response against both logging sinks.

members.title: Credential exposure in logs and the web UI log viewer: raw HTTPStatusError text puts the full request URL, including userinfo passwords and ?token= values, into the log output
members.problem: The old code logged only `exc.response.status_code`. The diff now logs the whole exception object. In the installed httpx, the HTTPStatusError message is built at httpx/_models.py:816 as "... for url '{0.url}'". `httpx.URL.__str__` returns the raw URI with userinfo left unmasked. The client keeps userinfo on request.url because _client.py:469 reads request.url.username/password to build BasicAuth. Config validation still accepts both leaking shapes: validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:112-157) checks only scheme, hostname and blocked IPs, so userinfo passes; reject_apikey_in_url (triggarr/models/config.py:65-89) rejects only keys that start with `apikey`, and its docstring says `?token=foo` stays valid for reverse-proxy setups. Concrete trigger: an instance url of `https://bob:s3cret@arr.example/` or `https://proxy/sonarr?token=abc` where /api/v3/system/status returns any non-401 error. The call path is startup.py:160 -> validate_connection -> the else branch at base.py:232. The log line then contains `s3cret` or `token=abc`. The redacting sinks (triggarr/logging.py:36-42 and 72-82) replace only values collected by startup.collect_secrets, so URL passwords and proxy tokens go unredacted to stderr and to log_buffer, which feeds the web UI log viewer. A 3xx response also adds the Location header to the message. The repo already has `_sanitize_exc` (triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44) guarding this property, and `_request_with_retry` (base.py:71-75) uses the same sanitization.
members.why_it_matters: A basic-auth password or a reverse-proxy token for the *arr instance gets written to persistent container logs and shown in the browser log viewer. This is the class of leak the project's SEC-02 and _sanitize_exc work was built to prevent.
members.fix_hint: Restore the status-only message, or log `_sanitize_exc(exc)`. If more detail is needed, add only `exc.response.reason_phrase` and leave the URL out.

members.title: Revert of named security fix reintroduces raw exception logging (CWE-532)
members.problem: This diff is a byte-for-byte revert of commit d47b4c2 (`fix(security): prevent potential key leakage in validate_connection log messages`), which deliberately replaced `exc=exc` with sanitized fields specifically to stop raw httpx/pydantic exception text from reaching logs. That fix was added even though triggarr/logging.py already had its custom redacting sink, so the maintainer judged the sink alone insufficient. The redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py:36-41) only does exact string-replacement of currently-configured secret values. The pydantic.ValidationError branch now logs str(exc); for a pydantic v2 missing-field error the string embeds the full input_value, which is the entire raw JSON body returned by the user's *arr instance. That log line also feeds the in-app log buffer rendered to the web UI log viewer (triggarr/web/routes.py:1195). For the httpx.HTTPStatusError branch the call site has no query params, so str(exc) would not carry the configured API key today; the demonstrated exposure there is weaker.
members.why_it_matters: This reopens a vulnerability the project already identified and fixed by name. The existing redacting sink is a narrow, exact-match secret scrubber, not a general log-sanitization layer, so full exception text now flows to stderr and the web log viewer unredacted.
members.fix_hint: Revert to the sanitized logging this diff undoes (status code / exc.error_count()), or if more detail is genuinely needed, log a sanitized summary (error type + field locations only, never raw input values / str(exc)).

This diff swaps the status-code-only log for the raw `exc`. str(HTTPStatusError) includes the full request URL, query string included. `_sanitize_exc`'s docstring says this kind of raw output is what the helper exists to prevent.

findings.title: validate_connection now logs the full pydantic ValidationError instead of the established error-count summary
findings.problem: The established convention for pydantic.ValidationError is to log only the error count: `_sanitize_exc` in triggarr/search/engine.py:42-43 returns `validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)` and is used at 6 call sites, and tracking.py:70-74 logs only the type name. Before this diff the code here followed that convention. Now it logs str(exc). Pydantic v2 puts `input_value=...` for each failing field into that string, so parts of the remote server's response body get echoed into the logs.

members.title: Data exposure: raw pydantic ValidationError text writes the *arr status response payload (input_value) to logs and the web UI
members.problem: `str(pydantic.ValidationError)` includes `input_value=` for each error, a truncated repr of the JSON body that was rejected. Before this diff only `exc.error_count()` was logged. Trigger: a reverse proxy, auth gateway or wrong subpath answers /api/v3/system/status with JSON that is not a SystemStatus. That body, including any session identifiers, internal hostnames or filesystem paths, is written to stderr and to the log_buffer shown in the UI. The redacting sink catches none of it unless it happens to equal an *arr API key. The codebase's own `_sanitize_exc` reduces this to `validation error (N issues)`, which is exactly what the removed code did.
members.why_it_matters: Upstream response bodies (internal paths, proxy or auth responses) reach operator-visible logs and the authenticated UI log viewer, which goes against the project's sanitization convention.
members.fix_hint: Keep the error count, or log field locations only (`[e['loc'] for e in exc.errors(include_input=False)]`). Do not log `str(exc)`.
